pages.title: Children & Families
pages.summary: Children and young people are encouraged to grow in Christian faith, with support for parents and families as they learn about God and share in the life of the church.
pages.welcomeText: The parish seeks to encourage children and young people to develop their own Christian faith, while supporting parents and families as they learn about God. The hope is that each person can grow in confidence, discover the gifts God has given them and find support for life’s challenges.
pages.welcomeAside: Children, students and young families are invited to share in a loving church community, where there is room for fun as well as learning about God.
pages.servicesIntro: The parish has described Family Services as worship shaped to be accessible across different ages. The approach is informal yet structured, with multimedia gospel presentations.

serviceDetails.text: Worship and presentations intended to be enjoyed by all ages
Multimedia used to support gospel presentations
Refreshments and time to catch up together afterwards

pages.servicesNote: For forthcoming service dates and times, use the live church calendar.
pages.schoolsIntro: The parish has welcomed two nearby school communities into the life of the Parish Church.

schoolCommunities.label: PARISH SCHOOL COMMUNITY
schoolCommunities.name: St Michael’s C of E (A) Infant School
schoolCommunities.description: The church has hosted monthly assemblies and special services. Assemblies at the school have also been led by the parish priest. The parish has described workshops associated with Mothering Sunday, Harvest Festival and Christingle.

schoolCommunities.label: SCHOOL COMMUNITY
schoolCommunities.name: RGS Surrey Hills
schoolCommunities.description: The school community has joined services in church and used the church for concerts and recitals.

pages.schoolsNote: For current school activities and arrangements, please contact the parish.
pages.seasonsIntro: Family worship and school workshops have been associated with moments in the church year, with creative activities and time to gather.
pages.seasonsNote: Check the Calendar for current services and events; dates and programmes can vary.
pages.firstVisitIntro: Bringing children is welcome. These pages can help you plan a visit and find current information.
pages.invitationText: Whether you are exploring church for the first time or returning with your family, you are warmly invited to find a service that suits you and be in touch if you have a question.

pages.title: Alpha Course
pages.summary: A welcoming space to explore the basics of Christian faith, ask questions and share your point of view.

sections.title: What is Alpha?
paragraphs: The parish describes Alpha as a series of sessions exploring the basics of Christian faith. It is for anyone who would like to explore, ask questions and share their point of view, whatever their background or context.

sections.title: What happens at a session?
paragraphs: The format described by the parish begins with tea and cake, followed by a short film presentation on a question about Christian faith and time for discussion. The course material explores topics including Jesus, prayer, faith, the Holy Spirit, the Bible and how God guides us.

sections.title: Who is Alpha for?
paragraphs: Alpha is intended for people who want space to explore Christian faith and ask questions. You do not need to have everything worked out before you come.

sections.title: Ask about a future course
paragraphs: The old website listed a course contact and dates that may no longer be current, so no course date or named contact is shown here. Please use the Contact page to ask whether a new course is planned.

pages.title: Fellowship & Bible Study Groups
pages.summary: Fellowship and Bible study groups are an important part of parish community life: a place to study the Bible, ask questions, share experiences and grow together.
pages.growingIntro: In a safe, confidential and non-judgemental setting, people can explore faith together, learn, ask questions and take part in one another’s lives.

themes.title: Explore the Bible
themes.text: Study Scripture together and make space for personal discovery and spiritual growth.

themes.title: Ask questions
themes.text: Share thoughts openly and learn alongside others in a safe, confidential and non-judgemental environment.

themes.title: Share life
themes.text: Talk about the joys and challenges of being a Christian in society today, and share refreshments.

themes.title: Build friendships
themes.text: Smaller meetings help relationships to develop, strengthening a sense of community and belonging.

pages.groupsIntro: Two regular Bible study groups meet weekly in Westhumble. Everyone is welcome.
pages.welcomeText: New members are always welcome. You do not need to be an expert in the Bible or theology to join. These informal groups are a chance to study, ask questions, share refreshments and get to know one another better.
pages.seasonalText: At particular seasons in life and in the church calendar, shorter fixed-length groups may also meet.
pages.contactText: Contact the parish office to ask about joining a Bible study group or to check the current arrangements.

pages.summary: The parish seeks to care for one another through spiritual support, practical help and encouragement.

sections.title: Care within the parish
paragraphs: The parish describes a community where people seek to share one another’s burdens and offer spiritual support, practical help and encouragement. The older team page listed a Parish Visitor role for pastoral care; the named contact may have changed.

sections.title: Privacy and safeguarding

pages.title: Our Vision
pages.summary: Inspired by God’s love, the parish seeks to grow spiritually, make Jesus Christ known and welcome people at the heart of the community.

sections.title: Inspired by God’s love
paragraphs: The parish vision is: “Inspired by God’s Love we seek to grow spiritually, make Jesus Christ known and be a loving, inclusive and welcoming church, at the heart of the community.”
This vision connects worship, spiritual growth, welcome and service in Mickleham and Westhumble.

pages.title: Our Churches
pages.summary: The Parish of Mickleham includes St Michael and All Angels in Mickleham and the Chapel of Ease in Westhumble.

sections.title: St Michael and All Angels, Mickleham
paragraphs: The parish describes St Michael and All Angels as a historic church at the heart of Mickleham, with Christian worship on the site for more than a thousand years. The church is listed Grade II* according to the old parish website. See Our History for the historical account.

sections.title: The Chapel of Ease, Westhumble
paragraphs: Westhumble is the parish’s second church. The old website describes the Chapel of Ease as a former barn and notes a much older chapel ruin further up the lane. See the Westhumble Chapel page for the existing account; details should be checked with the parish before a visit.

sections.title: Part of a wider benefice
paragraphs: The old parish welcome describes Mickleham as part of the United Benefice of Leatherhead and Mickleham within the Diocese of Guildford and the Church of England. Please confirm current organisational wording with the parish.

pages.title: Electoral Roll
pages.summary: The Church Electoral Roll is the parish’s formal list of lay members. It records a person’s connection with the parish and enables participation in parish governance.

sections.title: What is the Church Electoral Roll?
paragraphs: Each Church of England parish maintains an Electoral Roll. Being on the roll records a person’s connection with the parish and enables participation in parish governance, subject to the Church Representation Rules.

sections.title: Why join the Electoral Roll?
paragraphs: Membership gives a formal place in the life of the parish. It enables participation in the Annual Parochial Church Meeting and, where applicable under the Church Representation Rules, elections to the Parochial Church Council and wider Church synods. The application form explains the declarations required.

pages.title: Eco Church
pages.summary: Care for creation is part of the parish’s life and care for its churchyard. The Eco Group has encouraged practical steps for wildlife, the grounds and church life.
pages.quote: Reducing the causes of climate change is essential to the life of faith. It is a way to love our neighbour and to steward the gift of creation.
pages.awardContext: The Eco Group was established in 2022 to advise the PCC on local environmental action. The parish registered with the A Rocha Eco Church Award Scheme and received the Eco Church Silver Award. The supplied Churchyard Trail and award badge record this as a 2024 achievement; this page records the award received and does not claim that accreditation is currently active.
pages.alt: St Michael and All Angels Church viewed across its churchyard.
pages.imageCaption: The church and churchyard, pictured in the 2024 Churchyard Trail.
pages.journeyIntro: The parish’s source material records the following work by the Eco Group and volunteers.

initiatives.title: Hedgerow planting
initiatives.description: More than 80 metres of hedgerow were planted. The 2024 trail describes newly planted hedges around the newer churchyard as future green corridors for mammals and birds.

initiatives.title: Churchyard composting
initiatives.description: The compost area was reorganised so green waste could be composted and the resulting soil returned to areas within the churchyards.

initiatives.title: A small fruit orchard
initiatives.description: The Churchyard Trail records that an orchard was planted in winter 2022/23, with apple, pear, damson, quince and medlar trees.

initiatives.title: Garden of Remembrance
initiatives.description: Lavender and rosemary were planted around the Garden of Remembrance to provide summer nectar for insects.

initiatives.title: Wildlife-friendly mowing
initiatives.description: The trail describes the area behind the church being mown twice a year, and a three-year mowing and raking rotation in the newer churchyard, leaving areas unmown each year.

initiatives.title: Seasonal pond
initiatives.description: A rainwater-fed seasonal pond was created in 2024. The trail describes dragonflies, damselflies, pond insects and birds using the area.

initiatives.title: Information around the churchyard
initiatives.description: Information boards were installed to explain the changes taking place and why they matter.

initiatives.title: Reducing harmful chemicals and plastics
initiatives.description: The Eco Church page and trail describe work to phase out chemical herbicides and pesticides harmful to wildlife, and reduce new or single-use plastics. The trail says churchyard herbicide use had been phased out in favour of a weed burner for paving.

initiatives.title: Sustainable flower arranging
initiatives.description: The parish stopped using floral foam and trained flower arrangers to support stems with crumpled chicken wire instead.

pages.wildlifeIntro: These examples and counts are drawn from the supplied Churchyard Trail (2024) and the earlier Eco Church page. They are records from those sources, not a new survey.

wildlife.title: Four bat species
wildlife.detail: Serotine, Common Pipistrelle, Soprano Pipistrelle and Brown Long-Eared bats are recorded in the Churchyard Trail.

wildlife.title: 251 lichen species
wildlife.detail: The 2024 Churchyard Trail says 251 lichen species had been found in the churchyard.

wildlife.title: Slow worms
wildlife.detail: The trail records slow worms in the churchyard and explains the rotational mowing approach that leaves areas undisturbed.

wildlife.title: Pond and pollinators
wildlife.detail: The trail describes dragonflies, damselflies and pond insects at the seasonal pond, as well as birds using it.

wildlife.title: Earlier wildlife records
wildlife.detail: The earlier Eco Church page listed 120 flowering plants and 15 butterfly species in its first-year records; it said records for bees, birds, mammals and reptiles were still to be collated.

pages.trailDescription: Follow the churchyard trail to see the route, environmental work and wildlife described in the 2024 guide.

flowers.title: Creating Beauty, Sustainably
flowers.intro: For regular and occasional services, the parish encourages seasonal, locally sourced flowers and foliage, and the elimination of floral foam. Flowers are part of many important events; the guidance asks suppliers and arrangers to consider the environmental impact of their materials and the provenance of flowers.
details: The parish asks that floral foam, including the brand Oasis, is not used. Flowers can be arranged in water; the guidance points to sustainable mechanics for supporting stems and links to Sustainable Church Flowers for ideas and instruction.
The source guidance says that flower suppliers and floral creators may be asked about sustainability, provenance and air miles.
The source guidance discourages flowers in church during Advent and Lent. Anyone planning a wedding in either season is asked to speak with the Wedding Co-ordinator about what is appropriate.

pages.title: Safeguarding
pages.summary: The following policy was agreed at the Parochial Church Council (PCC) meeting in September 2026 and is reviewed annually.
pages.policyEntity: The Parochial Church Council (PCC) of St. Michael and All Angels Church, Mickleham (St. Michael’s)

sections.title: Our safeguarding commitments
paragraphs: This policy statement actively underpins all safeguarding work within the church.
In accordance with the Church of England Safeguarding Policy our church is committed to:
items: Promoting a safer environment and culture
Safely recruiting and supporting all those with any responsibility related to children, young people and vulnerable adults within the church
Responding promptly to every safeguarding concern or allegation
Caring pastorally for any victims/survivors of abuse and other affected persons
Caring pastorally for those who are the subject of concerns or allegations of abuse and other affected persons
Responding to those who may present a risk to others

sections.title: How the parish keeps people safe
paragraphs: The parish will:
items: Create a safe and caring place for all
Have a named Parish Safeguarding Officer (PSO) to work with the incumbent and the PCC to implement policy and procedures
Safely recruit, train and support all those with any responsibility for children, young people and adults to have the confidence and skills to recognise and respond to abuse
Ensure that there is appropriate insurance cover for all activities involving children and adults undertaken in the name of the parish
Display in church premises and on the Parish website the details of who to contact if there are safeguarding concerns or support needs
Listen to and take seriously all those who disclose abuse

Take steps to protect children and adults when a safeguarding concern of any kind arises, following House of Bishops guidance, including notifying the Diocesan Safeguarding Adviser (DSA) and statutory agencies immediately
Offer support to victims/survivors of abuse regardless of the type of abuse, when or where it occurred

Care for an monitor any member of the church community who may pose a risk to children and adults whilst maintaining appropriate confidentiality and the safety of all parties (after taking advice from the DSA)
Ensure that Health and Safety Policy, procedures and risk assessments are in place and that these are reviewed annually
Review the implementation of the Safeguarding Policy, Procedures and Practices at least annually

sections.title: Working together
paragraphs: Each person who works within this church community will agree to abide by this policy and the guidelines established by this church.

pages.title: Privacy & GDPR
pages.summary: This is the Data Privacy Notice of the Parochial Church Council (PCC) of St. Michael and All Angels Church, Mickleham.

documentHeading.controller: The Parochial Church Council (PCC) of St. Michael and All Angels Church, Mickleham (St. Michael’s)

sections.title: 1. Your personal data - what is it?
paragraphs: Personal data relates to a living individual who can be identified from that data (for example a name, address, email address, photographs or videos). Identification can be by the information alone or in conjunction with any other information in the data controller’s possession or likely to come into such possession. The processing of personal data is governed by the General Data Protection Regulation (“the GDPR”).

sections.title: 2. Who are we?
paragraphs: The PCC of St. Michael’s is the data controller (contact details below). This means it decides how your personal data is processed and for what purposes.

sections.title: 3. How do we process your personal data?
paragraphs: The PCC of St. Michael’s complies with its obligations under the GDPR by keeping personal data up to date; by storing and destroying it securely; by not collecting or retaining excessive amounts of data; by protecting personal data from loss, misuse, unauthorised access and disclosure and by ensuring that appropriate technical measures are in place to protect personal data.
We use your personal data for the following purposes:
items: To enable us to meet all legal, contractual and statutory obligations (which include maintaining and publishing our Electoral Roll in accordance with the Church Representation Rules).

To carry out comprehensive safeguarding procedures (including due diligence and complaints handling) in accordance with best safeguarding practice from time to time with the aim of ensuring that all children and adults-at-risk are provided with safe environments.
To enable us to provide a voluntary service for the benefit of the public in a particular geographical area as specified in our constitution.
To administer membership records.
To fundraise and promote the interests of the charity.
To manage our employees and volunteers.
To maintain our own accounts and records (including the processing of Gift Aid applications).
To inform you of news, events, activities and services running at St. Michael’s.

To share your contact details with the Diocesan office so they can keep you informed about news in the Diocese and events, activities and services that will be occurring in the Diocese and in which you may be interested.

sections.title: 4. What is the legal basis for processing your personal data?
items: Explicit consent of the data subject so that we can keep you informed about news, events, activities and services and keep you informed about diocesan events.
Processing is necessary for carrying out legal and contractual obligations in relation to Gift Aid.

items.text: Processing is carried out by a not-for-profit body with a religious aim provided:
children: the processing relates only to members or former members (or those who have regular contact with it in connection with those purposes), and
there is no disclosure to a third party without consent.

sections.title: 5. Sharing your personal data
paragraphs: Your personal data will be treated as strictly confidential and will only be shared with other members of the church in order to carry out a service to other church members or for purposes connected with the church. We will only share your data with third parties outside the parish with your consent.

sections.title: 6. How long do we keep your personal data?
paragraphs: We keep data in accordance with the guidance set out in the guide “Keep or Bin: Care of Your Parish Records” which is available from the Church of England website [see footnote for link].

Specifically, we retain electoral roll data while it is still current; Gift Aid declarations and associated paperwork for up to 6 years after the calendar year to which they relate; financial records for a minimum period of 7 years to support HMRC audits; Charity Commission audits and parish registers (baptisms, marriages, funerals) permanently.

sections.title: 7. Your rights and your personal data
paragraphs: Unless subject to an exemption under the GDPR, you have the following rights with respect to your personal data:
items: The right to request a copy of your personal data which the PCC of St. Michael’s holds about you.
The right to request that the PCC of St. Michael’s corrects any personal data if it is found to be inaccurate or out of date.
The right to request your personal data is erased where it is no longer necessary for the PCC of St. Michael’s to retain such data.
The right to withdraw your consent to the processing at any time.

The right to request that the data controller provide the data subject with his/her personal data and where possible, to transmit that data directly to another data controller, (known as the right to data portability), (where applicable).
The right, where there is a dispute in relation to the accuracy or processing of your personal data, to request a restriction is placed on further processing.
The right to object to the processing of personal data, (where applicable).
The right to lodge a complaint with the Information Commissioners Office.

sections.title: 8. Further processing
paragraphs: If we wish to use your personal data for a new purpose, not covered by this Data Protection Notice, then we will provide you with a new notice explaining this new use prior to commencing the processing and setting out the relevant purposes and processing conditions. Where and whenever necessary, we will seek your prior consent to the new processing.

paragraphs: To exercise all relevant rights, queries or complaints please in the first instance contact:

pages.title: The Church Building
pages.summary: Explore the historic fabric of St Michael and All Angels through the parish’s account of the building.

sections.title: Historic fabric
paragraphs: The parish history describes a church with early Saxon traces and substantial Norman and medieval fabric. Among the features it records are the chancel arch, chancel lancet windows, stone font, Norbury Chapel, medieval tombstones, carved pulpit and six bells.

The building has been altered over the centuries. Read the fuller Our History account for the parish’s notes on restorations and historic features. Please confirm current opening and visitor arrangements before making a special journey.

pages.title: The Churchyard
pages.summary: The churchyard is a place of remembrance and a part of Mickleham’s local history.

sections.title: A place of remembrance
paragraphs: The old parish website describes the churchyard as a place of beauty and historical value and points to a guide to its oldest part. It also publishes detailed churchyard regulations covering burials, memorials, flowers and the Book of Remembrance.

Those regulations were stated as approved by the PCC on 7 November 2023. Because local rules and availability can change, contact the parish for the current regulations, forms and advice before arranging a memorial, planting or burial.

pages.title: Churchyard Regulations
pages.summary: Ask the parish for the current approved churchyard regulations and forms before making arrangements.

sections.title: Current rules and advice
paragraphs: The previous parish website published regulations approved by the Mickleham Parochial Church Council on 7 November 2023. They cover burial eligibility, memorials, flowers, planting, cremated remains and the Book of Remembrance.
As these rules are locally approved and date-sensitive, this page does not reproduce them as current. Please contact the parish for the latest version and any required forms before taking action.

pages.title: Norman Architecture
pages.summary: The parish history identifies several Norman features within St Michael and All Angels.

sections.title: Features described in the parish history
paragraphs: The parish history describes the chancel arch as Norman, with chevron and dog-tooth ornament, and records the chancel lancet windows and stone font as early features. It places much of the present church in the Norman period, around the late twelfth century.

The same historical account describes earlier Saxon traces and later restoration. For context and the full story, see Our History. This page follows the parish account and is not a formal architectural assessment.

pages.title: Find Us
pages.summary: St Michael and All Angels is on Old London Road in Mickleham; Westhumble Chapel is on Crabtree Lane.

sections.title: St Michael and All Angels, Mickleham
paragraphs: Old London Road, Mickleham, Dorking, Surrey RH5 6DU, England.

The old parish visitor information describes a bike rack by the main entrance and the 465 bus stopping outside the church. It also says Box Hill & Westhumble station is about 1.4 miles away, a walk of around 30 minutes. Bus routes, facilities and journey times can change; check current travel information before setting out.

sections.title: Chapel of Ease, Westhumble
paragraphs: Crabtree Lane, Westhumble, Surrey RH5 6BG. The previous parish website gives this address. Please contact the parish if you need help confirming the precise entrance or current access arrangements.

sections.title: Map and access
paragraphs: Use the map link for directions to St Michael and All Angels. The website does not yet have verified information about step-free access, parking or facilities, so please contact the parish if you need access information before your visit.

pages.title: What to Expect
pages.summary: You are welcome to visit, take your time and join in with worship as much or as little as feels comfortable.

sections.title: A warm welcome
paragraphs: The parish welcomes visitors to its services and activities. You may take time to settle in, sit quietly, and ask someone if you need help.
Service formats vary. Check the Calendar for current service details, and contact the parish if you have a question about what to expect or need to confirm practical arrangements.

pages.title: Mickleham War Memorial
pages.summary: The war memorial stands in the churchyard at St Michael’s and commemorates local people who died in the two world wars.

sections.title: Remembering local history
paragraphs: The old parish website says the Mickleham War Memorial is in the churchyard of St Michael’s and bears the names of 11 men who died in the First World War and 11 who died in the Second World War. The Mickleham & Westhumble Local History Group produced an illustrated booklet with information about those commemorated.
The booklet and memorial details are linked from the earlier parish website. Contact the parish or local history group to confirm current access to the booklet.

pages.title: Parish Magazine
pages.summary: The parish magazine shares news and reflections from across Mickleham and Westhumble.

sections.title: News from across the parish
paragraphs: The old website linked to a current parish magazine edition and identified the magazine as a place for parish and village news. That issue link and editor contacts may now be out of date.

The new website’s News & Magazine section is ready to hold approved articles and updates. Use the News page for current published items; contact the parish if you are looking for a recent magazine edition.
